subtitle: When a Thin River Tested Two Proud Republics

panels.shot: sweeping aerial wide over a parched river between two clustered towns
panels.action: The Shakya–Koliya Mediator stands on a rocky bank between two facing assemblies across the dwindling Rohini, arms slightly raised, as dry fields and tense farmers stretch behind both sides under a harsh sun.

dialogue.text: In the hot plains between Kapilavastu and Ramagama, two kin-republics shared one thin river; when its waters fell, so did the mask of kinship.

i18n.hi: कपिलवस्तु और रामग्राम के तपते मैदानों में, दो रिश्तेदार गणराज्यों की एक पतली नदी साझी थी; पानी घटा, तो रिश्तेदारी का नक़ाब भी उतर गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from clouds down to the river winding between two settlements
panels.action: From high above, the Rohini River glints like a silver thread between two clusters of wooden halls and fields, the Mediator’s cloaked figure tiny on its bank, watching ox-carts move along both sides.

dialogue.text: This is the Rohini, a small river in the Nepal Terai. On one bank lived the Shakyas, on the other the Koliyas. They shared soil, seasons and blood… and soon, a quarrel remembered for centuries.

i18n.hi: यह रोहिणी है, तराई की छोटी नदी। एक तट पर शक्य रहते थे, दूसरे पर कोलिय; एक ही मिट्टी, मौसम और ख़ून… और जल्द ही, सदियों तक याद रखा गया झगड़ा।

panels.shot: medium wide of a Shakya assembly under a wooden hall
panels.action: The Mediator observes a Shakya republican council seated in a circle on mats in a timber hall, elders leaning on staffs, farmers with sunburnt faces standing behind, a clay map of the river scratched on the floor.

dialogue.text: The Shakyas were a gana-sangha, a small assembly-led republic. Elders and householders met in council-halls to decide on fields, roads, marriages… and, when needed, to send men to defend their boundaries.

i18n.hi: शक्य एक गण-संघ थे, छोटी सभा-शासित गणराज्य। बुज़ुर्ग और गृहस्थ सभा में खेत, रास्ते, शादियाँ तय करते… और ज़रूरत पर सीमाएँ बचाने के लिए लोग भेजते।

panels.shot: medium wide mirroring previous panel in a Koliya hall
panels.action: In a similar yet distinct wooden hall across the river, the Mediator watches Koliya elders in simple cloaks debate, while a young envoy stands with rolled palm-leaf records of irrigation channels.

dialogue.text: The Koliyas, too, were a republic. Like many small clans of the age, they balanced fields and spears, councils and kinship, while greater powers—Kosala, Magadha—shadowed the plains around them.

i18n.hi: कोलिय भी गणराज्य थे। उस युग के कई छोटे कुलों की तरह वे खेत और हथियार, सभाएँ और रिश्तेदारी संभालते, जबकि कोशल और मगध जैसे बड़े राज्य आस-पास मंडराते थे।

panels.shot: close-up on the Mediator’s face as he looks between two family groups
panels.action: The Mediator stands at a joint wedding feast under a fig tree, watching Shakya and Koliya families exchange garlands and gifts, a bride and groom seated shyly between them.

dialogue.text: Marriage tied the two sides. Tradition remembered how a Shakya prince, Siddhartha, took a Koliya bride, Yashodhara. The river was their boundary, but also their bridge.

i18n.hi: दोनों तट विवाह से बंधे थे। परंपरा कहती है कि शक्य राजकुमार सिद्धार्थ ने कोलिय वधू यशोधरा से ब्याह किया; नदी सीमा भी थी, और सेतु भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of green fields fed by a flowing canal from the Rohini
panels.action: The Mediator walks along a freshly cut earthen canal leading from the Rohini, watching farmers from both republics guiding water into embankments, children splashing in the flow.

dialogue.text: In the fifth century BCE, irrigation meant survival. Channels from the Rohini fed rice and millet. When the river ran full, Shakya and Koliya farmers laboured side by side, each trusting the other’s embankments.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं सदी ईसा-पूर्व में सिंचाई ही जीवन थी। रोहिणी से निकली नहरें धान और बाजरा सींचतीं; नदी भरपूर बहती, तो शक्य-कोलिय खेतों में कंधे से कंधा मिलाकर मेहनत करते, एक-दूसरे के बांधों पर भरोसा रखते।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide as the river shrinks, with a low angle sun blazing
panels.action: Under a scorching sun, the Mediator stands on cracked mud where water once flowed; the Rohini has shrunk to a shallow thread, with withering crops visible on both banks.

dialogue.text: Then came a lean season. Rains failed, the river shrank. What had been taken for granted—cool water in the channels—became a question with no easy answer.

i18n.hi: फिर दुबला साल आया। बारिश ने साथ छोड़ा, नदी सिकुड़ गई; जो बात तय मानी जाती थी—नहरों में ठंडा पानी—अब कठिन सवाल बन गई।

panels.shot: medium on a tense exchange between two groups of farmers at the canal head
panels.action: At the head of an irrigation channel, the Mediator stands between Shakya farmers blocking the inlet with a mud bund and Koliya farmers with spades raised in protest, their faces drawn and anxious.

dialogue.speaker: Shakya farmer
dialogue.text: Our fields lie upstream. We built this bund. We take the water first.

i18n.hi: हमारे खेत ऊपर हैं। यह बाँध हमने बनाया। पानी पहले हमारा हक़ है।

panels.shot: reverse angle focused on Koliya farmers with dry fields in the background
panels.action: The Mediator looks past the Koliya farmers to their parched fields, the soil cracked; one Koliya elder grips a staff, eyes burning with worry.

dialogue.speaker: Koliya elder
dialogue.text: If you take all, our children go hungry. Are we kin only in words?

i18n.hi: अगर तुम सब ले जाओगे तो हमारे बच्चे भूखे मरेंगे। क्या हम सिर्फ़ नाम के रिश्तेदार हैं?

panels.shot: medium wide of two separate councils meeting in agitation, split composition
panels.action: In a split scene, the Mediator watches on one side Shakya elders arguing with raised hands, and on the other Koliya councillors pounding their palms, both groups lit by flickering oil lamps.

dialogue.text: Early Buddhist texts preserve the memory of anger. Each side blamed the other. The quarrel over water twisted into words of insult, then into the language of honour and injury.

i18n.hi: आरंभिक बौद्ध ग्रंथों ने इस क्रोध को याद रखा। हर पक्ष ने दोष दूसरे पर डाला; पानी का झगड़ा अपमान के शब्दों में मुड़ा, फिर मान और अपमान की भाषा बन गया।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of armed men mustering at dawn on both banks
panels.action: At dawn, the Mediator stands on a rise as lines of Shakya and Koliya spearmen assemble on opposite banks of the Rohini, shields strapped, drums ready, the shrunken river between them like a scar.

dialogue.text: Men were mustered. Spears and leather shields came out of storage. A dispute born in the irrigation ditch had walked all the way to the riverbank, ready to cross into battle.

i18n.hi: आदमी जुटाए गए; भाले और चमड़े की ढालें भंडार से निकलीं। नाली में जन्मा विवाद नदी किनारे तक चलकर आ पहुँचा, जंग पार करने को तैयार।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot of the Mediator stepping forward between two advancing lines
panels.action: As both lines begin to advance, the Mediator steps down onto the dry riverbed, arms outstretched, his figure small but alone between two walls of armed kinsmen.

dialogue.text: Later tradition in Buddhaghosa’s commentary tells a different ending: not of slaughter on the Rohini’s edge, but of a mediator stepping between the ranks before the first spear was thrown.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा, बुद्धघोष की टीका, और अंत सुनाती है: रोहिणी के तट पर कत्लेआम नहीं, बल्कि एक मध्यस्थ, जो पहली भाला चलने से पहले ही दोनों पंक्तियों के बीच आ खड़ा हुआ।

panels.shot: close-up on the Mediator’s calm yet firm expression
panels.action: The Mediator’s face fills the frame, calm but intent, one hand raised as if to quiet both sides, the harsh light softening on his features.

dialogue.speaker: Mediator
dialogue.text: Which is worth more, kinsmen or water? Which loss can be mended?

i18n.hi: ज़्यादा क़ीमती क्या है—रिश्तेदार या पानी? कौन सा नुक़सान फिर से जोड़ा जा सकता है?

panels.shot: medium on two opposing captains lowering their weapons, exchanging uneasy glances
panels.action: On each bank, a Shakya captain and a Koliya captain look across the riverbed toward each other, shoulders easing as they slowly lower their spears, while the Mediator stands still between them.

dialogue.text: The commentary paints the scene as a lesson: the prospect of mutual loss cooling hot tempers. The words may be later, the exact dialogue uncertain, but the memory of avoided battle remained.

i18n.hi: टीका इस दृश्य को पाठ बनाकर दिखाती है: साझा नुक़सान की आशंका ने गरम दिमाग ठंडे किए। शब्द चाहे बाद के हों, संवाद चाहे अस्पष्ट हो, पर टली हुई लड़ाई की याद बची रही।

panels.shot: wide of both assemblies now seated on the dry riverbed in discussion
panels.action: Both Shakya and Koliya elders sit facing each other on the dry bed of the Rohini, staffs laid down, while the Mediator stands slightly aside, watching them speak with measured gestures.

dialogue.text: In the story, the two republics agree to share the flow and the repair of channels. Tradition holds this up as an example of restraint: a quarrel redirected back into rules and obligations.

i18n.hi: कहानी में दोनों गणराज्य बहाव और नहरों की मरम्मत बाँटने पर राज़ी होते हैं; परंपरा इसे संयम की मिसाल मानती है—झगड़ा वापस नियम और ज़िम्मेदारियों में मोड़ दिया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of the Mediator walking along the river with both sides’ farmers repairing bunds
panels.action: The Mediator walks between mixed groups of Shakya and Koliya farmers who together rebuild a damaged bund, sweat on their backs as they tamp the earth, the Rohini trickling past their ankles.

dialogue.text: What we know from the earliest texts is simpler and harder: neighbours quarreled over irrigation, and their anger worried those who taught non-violence and restraint.

i18n.hi: सबसे पुराने ग्रंथ बस इतना और कठिन बताते हैं: पड़ोसी सिंचाई पर भिड़ पड़े, और उनकी झुंझलाहट ने अहिंसा और संयम सिखाने वालों को चिंतित कर दिया।

panels.shot: broad historical montage with the Mediator superimposed over maps and ruins
panels.action: The Mediator’s silhouette stands against a faint map of the plains with names like Kosala and Magadha, overlaid with images of ruined mounds, forested stupas, and a distant hill-fort.

dialogue.text: Over time, both Shakya and Koliya republics vanished into larger kingdoms. Their council-halls fell silent. Yet their quarrel over a small river survived in monastic memory.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ शक्य और कोलिय दोनों बड़े राज्यों में विलीन हो गए; उनकी सभा-भवनों में सन्नाटा छा गया, पर एक छोटी नदी का झगड़ा मठों की स्मृति में ज़िंदा रहा।

panels.shot: ground-level wide at Ramgram stupa mound with modern archaeologists and the Mediator observing
panels.action: In the foreground, the Mediator watches present-day archaeologists carefully surveying a tree-covered mound identified with Ramgram, their equipment set up around the gentle rise under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: Near Ramgram, surveys have traced an ancient stupa tied by tradition to the Koliyas. At Tilaurakot and Piprahwa, debates continue over Kapilavastu’s exact ground. The river’s story still threads through living fields.

i18n.hi: रामग्राम के पास सर्वेक्षणों ने एक प्राचीन स्तूप ढूँढा है, जिसे परंपरा कोलियों से जोड़ती है; तिलौराकोट और पिपरहवा में आज भी कपिलवस्तु की सही ज़मीन पर बहस चल रही है—नदी की कहानी अब भी ज़िंदा खेतों के बीच से गुज़रती है।

panels.shot: serene wide of the Rohini at dusk, calm water reflecting both banks and the Mediator on the shore
panels.action: At dusk, the Rohini flows steady and quiet, reflecting the silhouettes of two distant villages; the Mediator stands on the bank, looking at the water with a thoughtful, almost questioning gaze.

dialogue.text: Shared rivers still run between neighbours. The Rohini’s old quarrel reminds us that laws and kinship are tested most sharply not by enemies, but by the thirst of those who live closest.

i18n.hi: साझी नदियाँ आज भी पड़ोसियों के बीच बहती हैं। रोहिणी का पुराना झगड़ा याद दिलाता है: क़ानून और रिश्तेदारी की असली परीक्षा दुश्मन नहीं, सबसे पास रहने वालों की प्यास लेती है।
